dataset.coverage: Full Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew and Aramaic XML, Strong and TWOT bridge index, part-of-speech map, and augmented Strong mapping.

evidence.claim: The repository files are released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International; the Brown-Driver-Briggs and Strong dictionary texts remain public domain; attribution should credit the Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible Project.
evidence.limitation: TWOT numbers are identifiers for reference only and the repository states that TWOT text is not transcribed.

evidence.claim: The pinned repository contains BrownDriverBriggs.xml, LexicalIndex.xml, BDBPartsOfSpeech.xml, and AugIndex.xml as the reviewed dataset paths.
evidence.limitation: The lexicon is described as a work in progress, so completeness and structural fidelity require deterministic validation.

evidence.claim: A complete scan of the 1906 Brown-Driver-Briggs Hebrew and Aramaic lexicon is marked public domain and can serve as a visual source-control reference.
evidence.limitation: The scan is not the machine-readable source and must not replace repository-level provenance or deterministic XML validation.

unresolvedQuestions: How completely does the current BrownDriverBriggs.xml reproduce every printed BDB sense and scripture reference?
How should incomplete or placeholder source nodes be represented without inventing missing source text?
How many H776 source nodes map losslessly to the existing 26-node Golden Reference hierarchy?
promotionRequirements: Compute and pin the canonical path-content fingerprint for all reviewed dataset paths.
Validate that all four files exist at the pinned commit and are free of symbolic-link or path traversal risk.
Build a dedicated deterministic OpenScriptures adapter without model-based structural inference.
Produce an H776 actual-source tree difference report before candidate generation is enabled.
